paper_metadata.title: State of art for sustainable machining of nickel-based alloys using coated and uncoated tools and machining of high strength materials using surface modified cutting tools

evidence.section: 2. Machining of nickel-based alloys using coated and uncoated tools
evidence.quote: Nickel based super-alloys are one such material category which meets all the requirements.

The use of coatings over the cutting tools sustainably reduces their wear and the same has been studied in the previous studies during the high speed machining of various nickel based, titanium based alloys

evidence.section: 2.1.1. Tool wear in dry machining of nickel based alloys
evidence.quote: Thakur and Gangopadhyay [30] during the dry machining of Inconel 825 for a cutting duration of 480 s observed BUE formation near the cutting edge

evidence.section: 2.1.1. Tool wear in dry machining of nickel based alloys
evidence.quote: Devillez et al. [31] reported that higher cutting speeds are not suitable for machining of Inconel 718 using coated carbide tools

evidence.section: 2.1.2. Cutting forces during dry machining of Nickel based alloys
evidence.quote: Koyi Lada et al. [44] during machining of Nimonic C 263 reported that PVD TiAlN/Tin coated tools led to a significant reduction in cutting forces

evidence.section: 2.2.2. Application of vegetable oils during machining of nickel based superalloys
evidence.quote: Chetan et al. [28] during machining of Nimonic 90 using Tin coated tools observed that the use of MQL during the process helps in increasing the length of cut for the tool by 200 mm and 250 mm

conditions.test_method: machining with coated tools under MQL

evidence.section: 2.2.2. Application of vegetable oils during machining of nickel based superalloys
evidence.quote: The tool life was found to be substantially increased by 10 – 22% in comparison to dry conditions.
